newsitem.title: POLAND: Non-banking share in Polish T-bill trade rises.
newsitem.headline: Non-banking share in Polish T-bill trade rises.

text.p: Advertising by banks and growing financial competence among corporates increased the share of non-banking clients in Polish T-bill purchases to 28 percent in 1996 from 15 percent in 1995, a finance ministry official said.

Piotr Dziewulski, the head of the public debt department, told a news conference on Friday that at the same time the share of banks in T-bill purchases fell to 66 percent this year from 75 percent last year.
"The financing (of the deficit) in the non-banking sector is desirable mainly because of its good influence on inflationary processes," Dziewulski said.
Foreign purchases of Polish paper also fell to seven percent of all T-bills in 1996 from 10 percent in 1995.

Turnover on the secondary T-bill market doubled to 5.18 billion zlotys in November from 2.62 billion zlotys in July with the number of transactions easing to 4,969 last month from 3,356 in July, the ministry said.

Dziewulski said the ministry focused on sales of 13-week, 26-week and 52-week paper this year with the 8-week and 39-week bills playing only an auxiliray role. He said the same policy was to be expected in 1997.
